summary: Alexander Studholme is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Paul Williams and Rupert Gethin.

Alexander W. Macdonald (1923–2018) worked in Tibetology and religious studies. He held posts at the CNRS (~1952–1988) and Paris Nanterre University (~1975–1993 as Professor), among affiliations with the University of Paris and Musée de l'Homme.

Alexander Wynne is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Bristol under Paul Williams and Rupert Gethin, earned a DPhil at Oxford under Richard Gombrich, and was a Junior Research Fellow at St John's College, Oxford.

Alexander Yiannopoulos works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and under supervisors and teachers including Karin Myers, Georges B. J. Dreyfus, Tom Tillemans, John J. Makransky, Jay L. Garfield, and others.

Alexander von Humboldt (1769–1859) studied at Frankfurt (Oder), Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne and Georg Christoph Lichtenberg, TU Bergakademie Freiberg, and the University of Jena, where he also held a post.

Alexander von Rospatt specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at UCL and the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, he held posts at Leipzig and Vienna, and later at the University of California, Berkeley.

Alexander von Staël-Holstein (1877–1937) was an Indologist, sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Tartu, Berlin, and Halle under Richard Pischel, he held posts at Saint Petersburg, Peking University (1918–1929), and the Sino-Indian Institute (~1930–1937).
Alexandra David-Néel (1868–1969) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Royal Conservatory of Brussels and under Philippe Édouard Foucaux and Kazi Dawa Samdup.

Alexandra van der Geer works in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied under Karel R. van Kooij, Leendert van Daalen, Henk Bodewitz, Fabio Martini, and Paul Y. Sondaar, and held a visiting post at the International Institute for Asian Studies.

Alexandre Langlois (1788–1854) was an Indologist who studied under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. He held positions at Lycée Charlemagne, Académie de Paris as an inspector, and the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (~1835–1854).

Alexis Sanderson is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at Oxford and under Swami Lakshman Joo. He was a Lecturer in Sanskrit (~1977–1992) and Professor (~1992–2015) at Oxford, and Emeritus Fellow at All Souls College.

Alf Hiltebeitel (1942–2023) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Haverford and the University of Chicago under J. A. B. van Buitenen and Victor Turner, before serving as a professor at George Washington University from 1968 onward.
Alf Sommerfelt (1892–1965) was a linguist who served as a professor of linguistics at the University of Oslo from 1931 to 1962.

Alfonsa Ferrari (1918–1954) was an Indologist and Tibetologist. She studied under Carlo Formichi, Giuseppe Tucci, Louis Renou, Jacques Bacot, and Marcelle Lalou, conducted research at the University of Rome, and taught Sanskrit there in 1952.

Alfred Bloom (1926–2017) was a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology scholar. After earning his Ph.D. at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi, he held posts at Oregon, the University of Hawaiʻi (1970–1986), and the Institute of Buddhist Studies (1986–1994).
Alfred Chilton Pearson (1861–1935) was a scholar of linguistics who studied at Christ's College, Cambridge, under John Peile.

Alfred Cooper Woolner (1878–1936) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Trinity College, Oxford. He served as Principal of Oriental College (~1903–1936) and held posts including Registrar and Vice Chancellor (1928–1936) at the University of the Punjab.

Alfred Cort Haddon (1855–1940) was a scholar in history and archaeology. Educated at Christ's College, Cambridge, he held posts at the Royal College of Science for Ireland (1880–1901) and the University of Cambridge (1879–1880; 1900–1926).
Alfred Edward Housman (1859–1936) studied at St John's College, Oxford (~1877–1881), and held an academic post at University College London from ~1892 to 1911.

Alfred Ernout (1879–1973) was a linguist who held positions at the University of Lille (1913–1924), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1924–1944), University of Paris (~1927–1946), and Collège de France (1941–1951).
